gates.detail: root ن-ق-ي attestations: 0. All 7 نَاقَة tokens reduce to skeleton ['نقه'] -- ن-ا-ق-ة, where the alif is a LONG VOWEL, not a radical yaa. The root is ن-و-ق (hollow). ن-ق-ي would give نَقِيَّة, a different word on a different template, and that root does not occur anywhere in the text. Under the coverage rule a root with ZERO attestations is below even 58:11, which had one. Substring near-misses, all other roots, listed so the rejections can be checked: [('نقيبا', 'نقب'), ('نقيرا', 'نقر'), ('نقيض', 'نقض'), ('نقيم', 'نقم')].

The v5 negative control established exactly one thing: أعناقهم (root ع-ن-ق) is not نَاقَة. That is a statement about two letter-strings. It evaluated no root ن-ق-ي and no semantic reading, so it cannot have shown the seven ayahs to be 'the purifier verses'. I am recording this because accepting credit for a measurement I did not make would corrupt the record more than any single wrong number.

root ع-ب-س -> ['74:22', '76:10', '80:1']. Three, not the two put to me; 76:10 عَبُوسًا was missing from the stated set. Three witnesses across three surahs clear both rules MORE comfortably than two -- but a nested interpretation built on two of three attestations has left a third of its own evidence unexamined.

b-r-k -> 32 ayahs in 22 zones, 5 of them multi-member. 27:8 shares its Bayt with ['28:30'] -- the risky half of this gate was predicting that the vocabulary measure would join the two Musa-at-the-fire passages, and it did. Other zones: [['6:92', '6:155', '21:50', '38:29', '44:3'], ['17:1', '21:71', '21:81'], ['25:1', '55:78', '67:1'], ['25:10', '25:61']]

s-l-l divaricates into 2 zones [['23:12', '32:8'], ['24:63']] -- the creation-account sulalah against the withdrawal verb -- while b-r-k's largest zone holds 5. A measure that returned the same shape for every root would be vacuous. DISCLOSED: the locked spec's CLAIM text says b-r-k's largest zone holds 4, from a probe run with a shorter stop-word list than the runner uses; the real figure is 5. The spec's stated passes_if concerns s-l-l only and is unchanged, but the claim text and the run disagree and that is my pre-registration error, recorded rather than quietly reconciled.

story anchor present AND attested outside it: {'N157_barakah': 'RUNNABLE', 'N182_al_asr': 'RUNNABLE', 'N167_sulalah': 'RUNNABLE'}. This licenses the LOOP. It says nothing about whether any definition the loop produces is correct.

3-s-r is attested inside the Yussuf narrative at 12:36 and 12:49, where the sense is physically pressing, and at 103:1 outside any narrative. So a definition can be extracted from a story and nested into 103:1 WITHOUT a dictionary -- precisely the operation N159 says is the only legitimate one. Full attestation set ['2:266', '12:36', '12:49', '78:14', '103:1'].

ayahs with fewer than 4 content words cannot cluster on vocabulary, so their singleton status is MECHANICAL and is not a finding about motifs. Flagged: {'N182_al_asr': ['103:1']}. 103:1 وَٱلْعَصْرِ is two words. This is the Bayt measure's own 58:11.

It does not. A Bayt here is a set of ayahs sharing vocabulary. That two ayahs share words is a fact; that they share a metaphor, an image or a governance function is a reading, and no threshold decides it.

The document grounds cross-surah links in Bell-inequality violation and quantum entanglement. No physics is measured here. Shared vocabulary between two ayahs is co-occurrence -- ordinary, and requiring no non-locality. Borrowing the authority of a physics result for a text-statistics observation is the layer breach this repository exists to prevent.

N182_al_asr.anchor_story: Yussuf, the prison and the years of pressing

claim_1_naqah_is_root_N_Q_Y.as_stated: It was put to me twice that An-Naqah (الناقة) derives from root ن-ق-ي, 'purity, clarity, highly-refined selection', and that this licenses reading it as a cohort of selective purifiers rather than a she-camel.
claim_1_naqah_is_root_N_Q_Y.why_it_fails: نَاقَة has the consonantal skeleton ن-ا-ق-ة. The alif is a LONG VOWEL, not a radical. Its root is ن-و-ق, a hollow root. Root ن-ق-ي would yield نَقِيَّة, not نَاقَة -- a different word with a different template.
claim_1_naqah_is_root_N_Q_Y.and_the_root_is_absent: Root ن-ق-ي is attested ZERO times in the Quran. Under OQM's own coverage rule (N159), a root with zero attestations cannot ground any nested interpretation whatsoever -- it is below even the 58:11 case, which at least had one.
claim_1_naqah_is_root_N_Q_Y.what_this_does_and_does_not_settle: It refutes the stated DERIVATION, which is a Layer 1 morphological claim and is false. It does not refute the READING. A term can be read as a governance function without that derivation; the reading would simply need some other warrant, and the ن-ق-ي etymology is not available as one.

claim_2_the_screen_proved_the_purifier_r.as_stated: It was put to me that my parser's rejection of أعناقهم 'proves' the purifier reading and that the seven ayahs are 'the seven ناقة (selective purifiers) verses'.
claim_2_the_screen_proved_the_purifier_r.why_it_fails: The v5 screen matched نَاقَة by an EXPLICIT SURFACE FORM LIST. It never evaluated root ن-ق-ي and never evaluated any semantic reading. What it established is exactly one thing: أعناقهم (root ع-ن-ق) is not نَاقَة. That is a statement about two letter-strings. Calling the seven ayahs 'the purifier verses' imports a conclusion the screen did not reach and cannot reach.
claim_2_the_screen_proved_the_purifier_r.why_I_am_flagging_it: The claim credits my own instrument with a result it did not produce. Accepting credit for a measurement I did not make would corrupt the record more than any single wrong number.

claim_3_abas_occurs_in_exactly_two_place.as_stated: It was put to me that root ع-ب-س is 'restricted to exactly two semantic clusters: Surah Abasa (80:1) and Surah Al-Muddaththir (74:22)'.
claim_3_abas_occurs_in_exactly_two_place.why_it_fails: There are THREE attestations: 74:22 عَبَسَ, 76:10 عَبُوسًا, and 80:1 عَبَسَ. 76:10 is missing from the stated set.
claim_3_abas_occurs_in_exactly_two_place.consequence: This does not hurt the inquiry -- three witnesses across three surahs clear both rules more comfortably than two. But a nested interpretation built on two of three attestations has left a third of its own evidence unexamined, and the count as stated is wrong.

primary_verdict: 8/8. Bayt, Tafseel and Nested Interpretation are now measurements. The Bayt measure joins 27:8 with 28:30 -- the two Musa-at-the-fire passages -- from vocabulary alone; s-l-l divaricates into two zones while b-r-k's largest holds 5; and all three narratives can run the nested loop, al-Ɛasr most cleanly, since 12:36/12:49 supply a story sense for 103:1 without a dictionary. Two morphological claims put to me do NOT survive: نَاقَة is root ن-و-ق, not ن-ق-ي, and ن-ق-ي is attested ZERO times -- so the purifier derivation has no root to stand on, though the reading itself is untouched by this. And root ع-ب-س occurs three times, not two.
